# New-ZbxDashboardWidget

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a dashboard widget for the -Widget of New-ZbxDashboardPage.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxDashboardWidget [-Type] <string> [-Name <string>] [-ViewMode <ZabbixWidgetViewMode>] [-X <int>] [-Y <int>] [-Width <int>] [-Height <int>] [-Field <ZabbixDashboardPageWidgetFieldRequest[]>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A widget is one tile of a dashboard page, such as a graph, a problem list or a clock, with its position, size and fields. The New-ZbxDashboardWidget cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -Widget of New-ZbxDashboardPage take as it is, alone or in an array. -Type is positional. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build a widget and put it on a new dashboard

```powershell
$clock = New-ZbxDashboardWidget -Type 'clock' -Name 'Server time' -X 0 -Y 0 -Width 12 -Height 3
New-ZbxDashboard -Name 'Ops overview' -Page (New-ZbxDashboardPage -Name 'Overview' -Widget $clock) |
    Select-Object DashboardId, Name
```

The builder writes one widget hashtable (type, name, position, size); it reaches the server inside a page (New-ZbxDashboardPage) of New-ZbxDashboard. 'clock' is the widget type name the frontend uses.

### Example 2: Configure a widget with fields

```powershell
$group = Get-ZbxHostGroup -Name 'Web servers'
$item = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -EQ 'app.requests'
$widgets = @(
    New-ZbxDashboardWidget -Type 'problems' -Name 'Web problems' -X 0 -Y 0 -Width 36 -Height 5 -Field @{ type = 2; name = 'groupids.0'; value = $group.GroupId }
    New-ZbxDashboardWidget -Type 'item' -Name 'Requests' -X 36 -Y 0 -Width 18 -Height 5 -ViewMode HiddenHeader -Field @{ type = 4; name = 'itemid.0'; value = $item.ItemId }
)
New-ZbxDashboard -Name 'Service status' -Page (New-ZbxDashboardPage -Widget $widgets) | Select-Object DashboardId, Name
```

-Field carries the widget's settings as (type, name, value) triples in the API's widget-field format: type 2 is a host group id and type 4 an item id; array fields are numbered (groupids.0, itemid.0).
